result: P. miniata larvae possess an extensive nervous system at 7dpf with serotonergic neurons concentrated in the anterior dorsal ganglia. Following bisection that removes these anterior serotonergic neurons, they regenerate at the anterior leading edge by 5dpb, are present in 12/15 larvae by 7dpb, and by 21dpb are bilaterally patterned resembling intact dorsal ganglia with extensive axonal projections.
evaluation: Claims C1-C8 provide converging evidence from immunostaining with validated markers (SynB, serotonin antibody), quantitative data across multiple time points (40/45 larvae show removal, 8/14 at 5dpb, 12/15 at 7dpb), and morphological characterization showing proper spatial patterning and neural morphology. The time series provides strong support for complete regeneration of the serotonergic nervous system.

result: Following bisection, embryonic neurogenesis gene expression states are reactivated in regenerating larvae. Axial patterning genes (foxq2, six3) and neurogenesis pathway genes (sox2, sox4, lhx2, elav) are sequentially re-expressed at the wound site and regenerating anterior in cells that would not normally express these markers, with sox2 upregulated by 1dpb, sox4 by 1dpb, lhx2 by 5-7dpb, and elav by 5-7dpb. Co-expression patterns (sox4/lhx2, lhx2/elav) and spatial localization recapitulate embryonic serotonergic neurogenesis pathways.
evaluation: Claims C9-C30 are well-supported by FISH data showing sequential gene expression, EdU co-staining demonstrating proliferation of progenitors, two-color FISH with 3D Imaris visualization confirming co-expression, and comparison to embryonic expression patterns from prior work. The spatial and temporal progression of gene expression strongly supports reactivation of embryonic neurogenesis pathways during regeneration.

result: Using a novel sox4:Kaede photoconvertible BAC reporter system, the authors demonstrate that new sox4+ neural progenitor cells are specified upon bisection. Green-only (newly expressing) sox4+ cells are observed at 2-3dpb in regenerating larvae, while photoconversion experiments show high numbers of new sox4+ cells in embryos (2dpf) but almost none in larvae (4dpf), indicating that sox4+ cell specification normally stops by 4dpf but is re-initiated by wounding.
evaluation: Claims C31-C44 are supported by experimental validation of the Kaede reporter system (7-day stability, recapitulation of endogenous expression), live imaging data showing distinct populations of green, red, and yellow cells, and quantitative comparison across developmental stages and regeneration (Figure 4F with statistical analysis). The photoconversion approach provides strong evidence for de novo specification of sox4+ cells upon injury.

result: Using sox2:Kaede and sox4:Cardinal double BAC reporters, the authors show that cells not previously expressing sox2 are induced to express sox2 following bisection, and a subset of these newly specified sox2+ cells co-express sox4 and enter neurogenesis pathways. These newly specified sox2+ cells contribute only to tissues normally derived from sox2+ lineages (ectoderm, mouth, ciliary bands, neurons), indicating they maintain normal embryonic lineage restriction and fate potential.
evaluation: Claims C45-C58 are supported by double BAC labeling experiments showing green Kaede+ Cardinal+ cells (4/15 larvae at 3dpb), lineage tracing through 7dpb showing neural projections, and examination of at least 10 larvae across three batches confirming lineage restriction. The observation that all sox4:Cardinal+ cells were red Kaede+ at photoconversion strengthens the inference that green Kaede+ Cardinal+ cells represent de novo sox2 expression followed by sox4 activation.

result: Treatment with 25 µM aphidicolin reliably blocks cell division (as confirmed by EdU staining) for up to one week with daily changes. In aphidicolin-treated regenerating larvae, green (newly expressing) sox2+ cells are still observed at the regenerating leading edge at 3dpb, demonstrating that new sox2 expression can be initiated in the absence of cell division and thus is not the result of asymmetric stem cell division.
evaluation: Claims C59-C62 are well-supported by dose-response experiments establishing effective aphidicolin concentration, time-course validation of sustained division inhibition (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), and live imaging showing green sox2+ cells in drug-treated larvae. This experiment provides strong evidence against a stem cell division mechanism and supports cellular respecification. The logic is sound: if new sox2 expression required asymmetric division, it should not occur when division is blocked.

result: The authors conclude that echinoderm larvae use dual mechanisms for nervous system regeneration: (1) induction of non-stem cells into ectodermal neural stem cells (de novo sox2+ cells) that maintain germline-restricted, multipotent fate (ectoderm and mouth ectoderm/endoderm), and (2) maintained lineages of existing sox2+ and sox4+ progenitors. This cellular plasticity, combining induced lineage stem cells with existing lineage-restricted stem cells, may underlie extensive regenerative capacity in echinoderms.
evaluation: Claims C75-C78, C84-C86 represent integrative conclusions supported by the lineage tracing data (C54-C56 showing lineage restriction, C85 showing yellow neurons from existing lineages) and the photoconversion experiments (C48-C52, C62 showing de novo sox2 induction). The conclusion is appropriately cautious about mechanisms ("possibly through dedifferentiation") and acknowledges that C86 is somewhat speculative. The dual mechanism model is well-supported by the data presented.

result: The manuscript provides extensive background context from prior literature on echinoderm regeneration, comparative regeneration mechanisms across taxa, embryonic neurogenesis in P. miniata, and the role of sox2 orthologs in pluripotency and cellular reprogramming in vertebrates.
evaluation: Claims C63-C74, C79-C83, C90-C96 are appropriately cited to prior literature and represent accurate summaries of established knowledge in the field. These claims provide necessary context for interpreting the current results but do not represent novel findings from this study.

result: The manuscript describes established technical properties and prior findings that support the experimental design: BAC constructs are stably inherited mosaically and co-integrate when co-injected; aphidicolin blocks DNA polymerase and cell division in echinoderms; serotonergic neuron numbers stabilize by 4-5dpf; and cell division localizes to the wound-adjacent anterior by 3dpb.
evaluation: Claims C87-C89, C97-C98 describe established technical knowledge (C87-C89) or cite prior work (C97-C98) that provides important methodological context. These are appropriately documented and support the interpretation of the experimental results.
